title: Ring volley
subtitle: Build a readable ring volley with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: Projectiles expand from the boss in every direction.
overview: Projectiles expand from the boss in every direction, testing radial spacing and the player’s ability to find or create a route through a closing circle.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a ring volley as one rule.

demo.title: Test the ring volley
phaseDescriptions: Charge energy around the complete emitter and show any deliberate gap before launch so the player reads a ring rather than unrelated shots.
Let the player pass through a gap, move with the expanding ring, block a limited section, or interrupt the charge if that counter is intended.
Once the expanding ring has crossed the playable route, emission stops and the boss pauses before producing another radial pattern.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Charge energy around the complete emitter and show any deliberate gap before launch so the player reads a ring rather than unrelated shots.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: Let the player pass through a gap, move with the expanding ring, block a limited section, or interrupt the charge if that counter is intended.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: Once the expanding ring has crossed the playable route, emission stops and the boss pauses before producing another radial pattern.

mistakes.title: A ring spawned directly on the player tests reaction latency instead of radial planning
mistakes.body: A ring spawned directly on the player tests reaction latency instead of radial planning.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible ring volley cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Tune projectile count and radius growth against arena size; gaps must remain wide enough at the distance where the player is expected to cross.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Offset consecutive rings, rotate their gaps, or vary expansion speed without hiding where each safe route begins.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: Once the expanding ring has crossed the playable route, emission stops and the boss pauses before producing another radial pattern.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: Projectiles expand from the boss in every direction, testing radial spacing and the player’s ability to find or create a route through a closing circle. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: Let the player pass through a gap, move with the expanding ring, block a limited section, or interrupt the charge if that counter is intended. Tune projectile count and radius growth against arena size; gaps must remain wide enough at the distance where the player is expected to cross.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: A ring spawned directly on the player tests reaction latency instead of radial planning. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
The complete player extent and the active region determine whether the route is real.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.
Escalation asks the player to apply the same learned rule under tighter constraints.
